rulings.Case Title: EST. OF DER HONG
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Report, Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required. The following issues to be cleared or addressed: (1) The petition continued to allege that there are no assets to distribute in this estate because all assets were administered and distributed in the husband's estate. However, the petition does not explain how the joint will resulted in joint administration of both estates. The husband's estate reported a 1/10 interest in the Spofford property and a 1/12 interest in the Grant property. The assets listed in the husband's I&A are subject to administration in the husband's estate. A petition brought under Prob. Code sec. 12250 to show that no assets were subject to this administration. (2) Need information on how these two properties were titled, specifically regarding Hong Der and Wai Fung Der's interests at the time of the decedent's passing. This vesting information will allow the Court to determine whether any assets were subject to administration in this estate. (3) Need clarification as to which will is operative for the decedent: the will dated 3/18/1975 or the will dated 8/15/1963. PARTIES APPEARING SHOULD CHECK IN FOR THE HEARING WITH THEIR FULL NAME. Counsel and parties may appear personally or remotely through Zoom or CourtCall. For a video appearance, go to zoom.us, click "join a meeting" and input meeting ID 160 225 4765 and password 514879. The Court prefers that counsel and parties appearing by video input their first and last name into the "Your Name" dialogue box. rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Accounting #1, Report, Fees
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 10/26/26. (No earlier availability.) No response to issues posted in the tentative ruling for the hearing on 7/1/26: (1) The amendments filed on 6/17/26 were not at least 15 days before the 7/1/26 hearing. (2) The only correct form of notice is the mandatory Judicial Council form Notice of Hearing, on the reverse side of which is the proof of service that should be completed. If a pleading form of proof of service is filed, the copy of the mandatory Judicial Council form Notice of Hearing that was served must be attached to the proof of service. [LRSF 14.1 C.6.] In addition, it appears that the conservator has already paid her attorney. Exhibit G to a declaration filed on 4/6/26 shows attorney fees paid out of an IOLTA account. Under what authority? Was there an order authorizing the fees? [CRC 7.755(a).] It also appears that the Guardian ad Litem never paid a filing fee for her "report" filed in the trust case on 3/3/25 that included a PETITION ("request") for her fees. That filing fee must be paid now. (No Notice of Conservatee's Death appears to have been filed.) Deadline is 10/12/26 to provide the assigned examiner courtesy copies of any papers filed to address these issues. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B.

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF CAROLE ANNE DERRY
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR PROBATE OF WILL AND FOR LETTERS TESTAMENTARY
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required for the judicial officer to review and determine: 1) whether petitioner has standing to proceed with this petition, as petitioner's second supplement indicates that: i) The decedent was survived by issue of great grandparents. (ii) The decedent's second cousins (35 in total identified by the second supplement) are entitled to succeed to this estate as relatives in the 6th degree and "next of kin" under Probate Code section 6402(f). iii) Petitioner, as a second cousin once removed and relative in the 7th degree, is not an heir as part of "the next of kin in equal degree" within the meaning of section 6402(f). iv) Absent a nomination from at least one of the second cousins: A) Petitioner has no priority for appointment under section 8465(a)(1) and (c). B) Petitioner may not even have any interest in this estate giving her standing to proceed with this petition as "any other person" in the lowest class of priority under section 8461(r), unless petitioner happens to be a creditor of the decedent under section 8461(q) in which case the public administrator would have to waive higher priority under section 8461(p) in favor of petitioner. 2) whether to accept petitioner's CRC 7.52(a) declaration of due diligence as sufficient to defer ascertaining paternal heirs of the decedent, and if so, whether to require retaining an heir search firm once petitioner is appointed and gains access to the estate funds and petitioning under section 11700 and LRSF 14.35(H) prior to final distribution to ascertain all paternal heirs. 3) whether to require an additional supplement disclosing all known issue of the maternal grandfather's parents or describing due diligence if they are not readily ascertainable, as: i) The second supplement only identified issue of the maternal grandmother's parents. ii) Issue of the maternal grandfather's parents, if they are relatives in the 6th degree, will share the estate as part of the next of kin in equal degree, and should receive notice of this petition. PARTIES APPEARING SHOULD CHECK IN FOR THE HEARING WITH THEIR FULL NAME. Counsel and parties may appear personally or remotely through Zoom or CourtCall. rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF HERRITO W HUI
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR SPOUSAL PROPERTY
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required, although item 1 of the DE-120 form filed on 08/18/2026 did not refer to the "amended" petition, and proof of service shows notice was given on 08/15/2026, before the amended petition was filed on 08/18/2026. See CRC 7.53(a) and LRSF 14.14(A). If the hearing on this petition is to proceed on the merits, the judicial officer is to review and determine whether sufficient evidence has been submitted in support of the proposed finding that the subject real property was community property. The decedent and petitioner, husband and wife, took title to the property as tenants in common. The petition requests an order only confirming petitioner's interest in the property as one-half share of community property belonging to petitioner as the decedent's surviving spouse. The petition does not request an order determining that the decedent's interest in the same property passed to petitioner as the decedent's surviving spouse and sole heir entitled to succeed to the decedent's one-half share of community property without administration. The form of title controls at death, and the community property presumptions under Family Code sections 760 & 2581 do not apply in probate cases. See In re Brace (2020) 9 Cal.5th 903, 934; see also Estate of Wall (2021) 68 Cal.App.5th 168, 175. Property cannot be held both as community property and tenants in common at the same time, and each spouse's tenancy-in-common interest is his or her separate property. See Estate of Mitchell (1999) 76 Cal.App.4th 1378, 1385. As the decedent and petitioner's tenancy-in-common interest in the property is presumed to be his or her separate property, Evidence Code section 662 applies and requires clear and convincing evidence to rebut the title presumption. The only allegation purporting to support the community property characterization of the property is that the decedent and petitioner "definitely believed that they were responsible for undivided interests and liabilities in the property when they acquired the premises at 2646 San Jose Ave in June 1999".
